image_description: A group of sea lions resting on a wooden dock structure. The central subject is a brown sea lion sitting upright, facing forward with its head tilted up. To the left, another sea lion lies on its back/side. In the background and foreground right, parts of other sea lions are visible. The setting appears to be a sunny outdoor pier.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is broad with prominent sagittal crest in males.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The central subject's head shape is somewhat rounded and lacks the distinct, rugged sagittal crest typical of mature male sea lions; it resembles a female or juvenile more than a dominant male.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: External ear pinnae (visible ear flaps) distinguish from true seals.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Small but distinct external ear flaps are visible on the side of the central sea lion's head, confirming it is an otariid (sea lion) and not a phocid (true seal).
While sea lions have whiskers, they are not clearly resolved or 'prominent' in this image due to lighting and resolution; the snout area appears smooth rather than showing distinct vibrissae.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Foreflippers are large, broad, and hairless on underside used for terrestrial locomotion.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The foreflipper of the central subject is visible, appearing large and broad. The texture suggests the leathery skin typical of the underside.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Hind flippers can rotate forward for walking on land.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The hind flippers are largely occluded by the body position and the angle of the shot; their rotation capability cannot be visually verified in this static pose.
